items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the retirement and social security law, in relation to transfer of retirement membership for certain employees of SUNY within the professional, scientific and technical bargaining unit
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S6435

 TITLE OF BILL :

An act to amend the retirement and social security law, in relation to
transfer of retirement membership for certain employees of SUNY within
the professional, scientific and technical bargaining unit

 PURPOSE :

To allow certain employees, who are participants in the Optional
Retirement Program (ORP) established pursuant to article 8-b of the
New York State Education Law, to join the New York State and Local
Retirement System (ERS) or the New York State Teachers Retirement
System (TRS) and to purchase credit for past-service accrued while
participating in the ORP.

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :

Section 1 of the bill defined an "eligible employee" as an individual
who, as of the effective date of this Act, is an active employee of
the State University of New York (SUNY) in the professional,
scientific and technical bargaining unit, a participant in the ORP,
who is a registered nurse first employed of SUNY Stony Brook Hospital
between the dates January 1, 1996 and December 31, 1999, and as of the
date of their transfer application, is still an active SUNY employee.
Such eligible employees must submit an application for membership in
ERS or TRS no later than December 31, 2018.

Section 2 provides this act shall take effect immediately.

 JUSTIFICATION :

The SUNY Optional Retirement Program is a defined contribution plan
and was established in 1964 as an alternative retirement option to
membership in ERS and TRS. All full-time employees in the unclassified
service are eligible to participate in the optional plan; should a
member fail to elect participation, they are be automatically placed
in ERS or TRS depending on title.

Under current law, should an optional plan participant leave SUNY and
commence employment with another New York State agency and thus become
a member of ERS or TRS, they will not be permitted to establish credit
for any service for which the state contributions under the optional
plan were made on their behalf.

This bill would allow individuals to both apply for membership in ERS
and/or TRS and to purchase past-service credit for the period of time
the eligible employee participated in the ORP.

 PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :

TBD.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
Immediately.
